messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: rollout 'rollout-canary-alpha' smart-routing detected elevated 5xx from canary variant 'chat-alpha-canary' (>25% over 90s). Fallback engaged to 'chat-omega-stable' with sticky pins. Region mismatch spikes observed between ap-southeast-1 <-> eu-central-1. Paging @oncall.

nina: seeing the spike on grafana. Canary instances show memory thrashing + queue timeouts around 01:02 UTC. Latency graphs for affected routes go from ~120ms -> 2s.

alex.t: linking routing policy: rollout/rollout-canary-alpha. Policy has sticky_fallback=true and sticky_scope=global. That global scope means clients retried in other regions still map to pinned variant.

rafael: CS reports one large tenant seeing degraded completions and increased token cost due to retries. They've DM'd logs to cs-team.

alex.t: probable interaction: canary underprovisions KV cache for longer contexts -> OOM or evictions -> >5xx -> fallback pins sessions to stable -> because pins are global, retries from different region route to other cluster which thinks it's new and triggers fallback back to canary under some conditions -> oscillation.

oncall: suggest immediate actions: 1) pause rollout 2) disable sticky_fallback or set TTL=0 3) purge pinned sessions 4) throttle canary traffic if pause not possible.

devops-bot: command ok: POST /api/v1/rollouts/rollout-canary-alpha/pause -> accepted @1925567925

oncall: paused via API. Response: {"id":"rollout-canary-alpha","status":"paused","updated_by":"oncall"}

nina: executing policy change to remove sticky on fallback:
```
rwctl routing patch --policy rollout-canary-alpha --set sticky_fallback=false
rwctl routing patch --policy rollout-canary-alpha --set sticky_ttl=0
rwctl sessions purge --policy rollout-canary-alpha
```

ops-bot: routing service acknowledged changes; session purge returned 200 with count=1342 pins cleared @1925567998

alex.t: logs from canary pods (sample):
```
2026-03-15T01:01:16.123Z ERROR inference::kv_cache Unable to reserve kv_cache bytes=980MB for req=zx9kl
2026-03-15T01:01:16.125Z WARN runtime::queue request wait_time_ms=2400 req=zx9kl
2026-03-15T01:01:16.126Z ERROR request::response 5xx inference_failure variant=chat-alpha-canary req=zx9kl
```

rafael: customer notified: "We've paused the canary and cleared routing pins; investigating root cause and will update in 30 minutes." They acknowledged and asked for impacted session ids.

oncall: monitoring: cross-region routing count back to baseline in last 90s. Canary instance error rate still elevated for canary-only traffic but global user errors down ~65%.

nina: also found a quota change in the canary model config: kv_cache_limit=1GB, production expected 1.6GB due to longer contexts. That change likely introduced allocation failures for some user loads.

alex.t: mitigation plan (short term): keep rollout paused, revert kv_cache_limit in canary to last-known-good, add rate limit on long-context requests to canary group. Medium term: add pre-deploy validations for memory plan mismatches and prevent sticky_fallback when backend error rate > 15%.

devops-bot: executed config revert on canary model: set kv_cache_limit=1.6GB by rafael @1925568290 -> response ok.

oncall: reran health checks. Canary instances restarted and memory allocations look normal on first pass. Will keep paused but monitoring for 10m before resuming any traffic.

cs-team: preserving customer logs and transcripts; saving to secure path /secure/incident_snapshots/rollout-canary-alpha/1925567890/

nina: adding runbook actions in thread:
- action: revert canary memory plan (assignee: rafael)
- action: add automated gate preventing sticky_fallback when variant error_rate > 15% (assignee: alex.t)
- action: postmortem + customer timeline within 48h (assignee: nina)
- action: update rollout policy docs for sticky scope implications (assignee: platform)

alex.t: one extra note: make sticky scope regional-only by default to avoid global cross-region oscillation. Filing RFC.

ops-bot: handoff: oncall -> night-sre @1925571290

oncall: handing off monitoring to night-sre. I set an alert to escalate if canary error rate >10% or region handoffs reappear. Leave this thread for follow-up.

incbot: Incident mitigated: immediate controls applied (pause, purge pins, revert memory plan). Severity SEV2 -> monitoring. Postmortem scheduled.
